title: llama-swap · inference
description: Inference metrics for llama-swap: tokens, throughput, cache and spec-decode efficiency, and model swap behaviour. Fed by llamaswap-exporter (:9820), not by llama-swap's own /metrics endpoint, which is host/GPU telemetry only and duplicates node_exporter and dcgm/rocm-exporter.

panels.title: Generation throughput
panels.description: Tokens per second the fleet is actually emitting, summed across every model and host. This is the headline number — it is real output, not capacity.

panels.title: Models resident
panels.description: Models with a live llama-server process across the selected hosts.

panels.title: Error ratio
panels.description: Non-2xx share of requests. 400s here are usually malformed client payloads (bad vision requests), not model failures.

panels.title: llama-swap API
panels.description: 0 if the exporter cannot poll llama-swap on any selected host — which means inference on that host is down.

panels.title: Rows lost (1h)
panels.description: Requests the exporter provably missed because llama-swap's 1000-row activity buffer lapped between polls. Non-zero means POLL_INTERVAL is too long on that host and token counters are undercounting.

panels.title: Generation speed by model (p50)
panels.description: Median per-request generation speed. A model dropping here without a config change has usually spilled out of VRAM into system RAM.

panels.title: Prompt speed by model (p50)
panels.description: Median prompt-processing speed. This is where flash-attention and rocWMMA regressions show up first — see the b10154 note in config.yaml.

panels.title: Tokens generated by model
panels.description: Stacked so the total is the fleet's real output and each band is one model's share of it. Contrast with the p50 panel: that is how fast a model runs, this is how much work it actually did.

panels.title: Generation speed spread (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Fleet-wide spread across the current selection. A widening gap means some requests are being served far worse than the median — usually contention between concurrent slots.

panels.title: KV cache hit ratio by model
panels.description: Share of prompt tokens served from KV cache rather than reprocessed. Low values on a conversational workload point at cache thrash — often another model evicting this one.

targets.expr:
sum by (model) (rate(llamaswap_cache_tokens_total{instance=~"$instance", model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
/ clamp_min(sum by (model) (rate(llamaswap_input_tokens_total{instance=~"$instance", model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.0001)

panels.title: Speculative decode accept rate
panels.description: Fraction of draft-model proposals the target model accepted — whether speculative decoding is earning its VRAM. Empty on hosts whose llama-swap build predates the draft token fields (pre-v243).

targets.expr:
sum by (model) (rate(llamaswap_draft_accepted_tokens_total{instance=~"$instance", model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval]))
/ clamp_min(sum by (model) (rate(llamaswap_draft_tokens_total{instance=~"$instance", model=~"$model"}[$__rate_interval])), 0.0001)

panels.title: Request duration by model (p95)
panels.description: Wall clock, so this includes queueing and any model load the request had to wait for — not just generation time.

panels.title: Busy slots (fleet)
panels.description: Slots actively decoding across the fleet right now. This is a sampled gauge, not a counter: requests shorter than the 15s scrape interval can fall between samples, so treat it as a read on sustained concurrency rather than an exact request count.

panels.title: Slot utilisation by model
panels.description: Busy slots as a fraction of the slots the model was started with (-np). Sitting near 1.0 means requests are queueing behind full slots and -np is the bottleneck, not the GPU.

panels.title: KV cache occupancy by model
panels.description: Tokens held across all slots versus total KV capacity. Climbing toward 1.0 means slots are about to start evicting cached prefixes, which shows up as the cache hit ratio falling and prompt speed dropping.

panels.title: Busy slots by model
panels.description: Absolute busy slots against the capacity line for each model. Same unit on one axis deliberately — the gap between the two lines is the headroom, and that is the thing worth reading.

panels.title: Context window per slot
panels.description: What ONE request actually gets. llama.cpp splits a model's context across its -np slots, a model started with -np 8 over 131k context gives each request only ~16k. A request longer than this is truncated no matter how large the model's total context looks.

panels.title: Model residency
panels.description: Which models were resident, when. Reading this next to the throughput panels is how you attribute a latency spike to a swap rather than to the model itself.

panels.title: Swap transitions per hour
panels.description: Load/unload transitions per host per hour. Every swap is a full model reload from disk. Sustained high values are the failure mode that quietly destroys throughput without surfacing as an error anywhere.

panels.title: Model summary over the selected range
panels.description: Fleet-wide totals per model over the dashboard time range, aggregated across hosts — filter with the Host variable to narrow it. The models sitting at zero are config entries nothing actually calls; this is the panel that tells you which ones to retire.

panels.title: Rows lost & llama-swap restarts
panels.description: Lost rows mean undercounted tokens — lower POLL_INTERVAL on that host. An id reset is llama-swap restarting, which is expected after a config change and suspicious otherwise.

panels.title: Poll duration
panels.description: Should sit in the low milliseconds. Hosts on pre-v243 builds run high, because those builds ship the entire 1000-row buffer on every poll.
